subject: Clarify: how streaming + long-context sessions count toward minimums and discounts
messages:
From: Carlos Mendez <c.mendez@vantageai.com>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 30 Jun 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Question on streaming + long-context billing minimums

Hi Soojin,

Quick question as we're finalizing the SOW (attached): our engineering team plans to use a mix of long-context sessions (pinning a 100k-token context per customer for retrieval-augmented generation) and streaming generation for chat UI. We have two billing-related uncertainties we need clarified before procurement signs: 

1) If a client opens a long-context session that stays warm (KV cache) but only issues a single short streaming request later, do we pay for the entire context-length window or only for the tokens emitted in the streaming call?
2) Streaming responses are chunked on the wire — do you meter/round per chunk, per-second of stream, or per-total tokens produced? How do minimums apply (we saw mention of per-call minimums in the quote but not for streaming).

For negotiations, procurement is asking for concrete examples where we hit the committed spend and where we might be charged banked minimums that wouldn't count toward committed usage. We also want to understand whether caching (prefix/KV cache) yields credits against per-token charges.

Attaching the SOW and a short example spreadsheet. Thanks,

—Carlos
Procurement
Vantage AI

Attachments: SOW-VantageAI-draft.pdf (PDF, 120KB), billing-examples-v2.xlsx (Excel, 34KB)

From: soojin_lee@redwood.ai
To: Carlos Mendez <c.mendez@vantageai.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 30 Jun 2025 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Question on streaming + long-context billing minimums

Carlos — thanks for the clear examples and for sending the SOW. Looping in Ben (sales) and Marissa (finance) to confirm the precise language we should include in the SOW.

Short answers up front:
- Long-context "warm" sessions: you are only billed for tokens that are actually processed/used for generation. The pinned context that lives in KV cache does not continuously accrue token charges just by being present; charges occur on read/usage at model runtime (e.g., when the model attends to cached prefixes it will bill the tokens that the model processes for that request).
- Streaming: we meter by produced tokens, but there is a per-call minimum applied to the request type. For streaming responses we translate streaming activity into token units and then apply the rounding/minimum rules. There are edge cases (very short streams + long pinned contexts) where rounding to the minimum can feel punitive — Ben, can you add the numeric examples and how committed spend gets credited?

Proposed next step: Ben and Marissa to share a worked example (three scenarios) and a suggested SOW clause that clarifies how minimums/credits apply. After that, we can put the clause into section 2.4 of the SOW and re-share.

Thanks,
Sooin
Director, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

To: soojin_lee@redwood.ai, Carlos Mendez <c.mendez@vantageai.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 30 Jun 2025 11:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Question on streaming + long-context billing minimums — worked examples

Folks — I ran the three scenarios you mentioned and included a short table in the attached spreadsheet. Summary below (numbers are illustrative and map to the quote in RDW-9421):

Scenario A — Warm long-context session, single short streaming reply
- Context pinned: 100k tokens (not billed while idle).
- Request: client issues a single streaming prompt that causes the model to read a 1k-token window from KV and stream 120 tokens back.
- Metering: we bill for (tokens read by model) + (tokens produced). In this case: 1,000 (attended context) + 120 = 1,120 tokens.
- Rounding/minimums: per our quote, usage is rounded up to the nearest 100-token billing quantum for enterprise SKUs. So 1,120 -> 1,200 tokens billed.
- Commit credit: billed tokens count against committed usage after rounding.

Scenario B — Very short stream; long pinned context not read
- Context pinned: 100k tokens (idle).
- Request: client sends a metadata ping that produces 6 tokens in response and does not require reading the pinned context.
- Metering: tokens produced = 6. Rounding to 100-token quantum => 100 tokens billed.
- Commit credit: 100 tokens count toward committed usage. The effective waste is why customers sometimes ask for a "stream minimum cap" in the contract.

Scenario C — Long streaming session with many small chunks
- Model produces 2,400 tokens across a streaming session in 50 chunks. We aggregate the produced tokens and bill on the total produced tokens per request (not per chunk). So the rounding is applied to the session total (2,400 -> 2,400), no per-chunk penalty.

Other notes:
- Caching credits: we offer a small prefix cache credit program for customers on enterprise committed plans. If your workload frequently re-attends the exact same 1k token prefix within a 24-hour window, we can apply a cache-hit credit that reduces billed attended tokens by up to 60% for those repeated reads. This is offered as a negotiated addendum and appears as a line item credit on the invoice.
- Hybrid minimums: For customers with a committed spend, we can apply a blended minimum where small per-call rounding is capped monthly so excessive rounding waste is netted off against committed usage (i.e., we cap monthly rounding overhead at X% of committed spend). This is part of the deal negotiation (RDW-9421 currently proposes 2% cap).

Marissa — can you confirm how we present the rounding cap in the SOW and the invoice language (one-line description + example calculation)?

Ben
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachments: billing-examples-v2.xlsx (updated)

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: ben_carter@redwood.ai, soojin_lee@redwood.ai, Carlos Mendez <c.mendez@vantageai.com>
Date: Tue, 01 Jul 2025 09:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Question on streaming + long-context billing minimums — SOW language

Carlos / team — I drafted suggested contract language below to put into section 2.4 of the SOW (I added it to the attached SOW as well). Please review and tell me if this is sufficiently explicit for procurement.

Suggested clause (plain language):
"Billing units for model inference are calculated as the sum of tokens attended by the model (including tokens read from KV/prefix cache) plus tokens produced by the model. Usage is aggregated per API request and rounded up to the nearest 100-token billing quantum for Enterprise SKUs. For streaming requests, tokens produced across the streaming session are summed and rounded once per session; the provider does not round per-network-chunk. Pinned contexts that remain idle do not generate token charges until they are read by the model for a request.

Customers on committed plans receive a monthly rounding-overhead cap equal to 2% of the committed monthly token spend; any rounding overhead beyond this cap will be credited back as a line-item credit on the next invoice. Additionally, customers may negotiate prefix-cache credits (up to 60% reduction on repeat-attended tokens for qualifying workloads), which will be listed as a bill-level credit when applied.
"

If that reads ok, Soojin / Ben, I propose we attach a 3-row example table to section 2.4 showing Scenario A/B/C (numbers from Ben's email) so procurement can see the arithmetic.

Carlos — if procurement is OK with the 2% rounding cap and wants the cache-credit option, we can add a sub-bullet tying the cache-credit eligibility to usage patterns and a 90-day evaluation window.

Marissa
VP, Finance Operations
Redwood Inference
